articles.title: Relation algebra is not relational algebra
articles.summary: Relation algebra is a CS concept that is equivalent to domain-independent relational calculus, a well-behaved fragment of first-order logic queries. It is also equivalent to FOL3, which restricts first-order logic to use at most three different variables. However, it can be extended to match the expressive power of FOL with a fork operator. This concept has been quietly finding applications in computer science, including the Alloy analyzer, a database system that uses it as "relational logic".
